source.note: The repository is public and pre-release: it has no release tag and nothing is published to a package registry, so every profile is a clone of the repository at the pinned commit. The dependency release tags are the pins in pins.toml; the verified profiles do not need them.

verifier.reason: Re-verification of a run's evidence in a separate process (`redevops-qa verify`: the same code the run used, so not independent of the harness and the libraries, and the hash chain it checks is unkeyed) is installed and run only by the profile local-python-qa (Playwright Chromium and Robot Framework, Linux x86_64); no other profile installs it, and an engine's own pass or fail is not a verdict.

docker-compose.disabled_reason: Docker Compose files ship in deploy/standalone and the image is published (ghcr.io/redevops-io/redevops-qa:0.6.2) and was installed from the published reference with those files on one host, but the profile stays planned: a profile is offered only when a named CI job of tests.yml runs it through tools/run_install_profile.py, and these profiles describe a Python checkout with a closed set of commands (git, python); no such job installs from the published image yet, and the standalone job builds the image from the commit instead.

kubernetes-helm.disabled_reason: Kustomize manifests (there is no Helm chart) ship in deploy/standalone/k8s and were applied to a throwaway local cluster with the arm64 image, and the image is published (ghcr.io/redevops-io/redevops-qa:0.6.2), but the profile stays planned: a profile is offered only when a named CI job of tests.yml runs it through tools/run_install_profile.py, and no job applies the manifests to a cluster; the lanes were not run in a cluster. The cluster checks in qa-checks inspect other people's manifests and are not a deployment of this runtime.

profiles.title: ReDevOps QA in a local Python environment: the pinned bundle, the Playwright Chromium and Robot Framework lanes, and the verifier
prerequisites: Python 3.12 available as `python3.12` with the `venv` module (Debian and Ubuntu: the `python3.12-venv` package). The bundle is built for CPython 3.12 and install.sh refuses any other minor.

The bundle archive and its `.tar.sha256` file in one directory (`bundle_dir`): built from a checkout of https://github.com/redevops-io/redevops-qa with `python tools/build_bundle.py build --out DIR`, or taken from a workflow run. No bundle is published. Compare the sha256 of the archive with a value you obtained from somewhere its producer does not control.
bash, tar, and root or sudo for the browser step's `--with-deps` (it installs the operating system libraries Chromium needs with apt).

Network access to the Playwright download host for Chromium (the browser is not in the bundle; its archives are checked against sha256 values pinned in the bundle before they are unpacked). Nothing else is downloaded by these steps: the wheels are installed from the bundle with `--no-index --require-hashes`.
All commands are run from one working directory, using a POSIX shell.

source.title: Check that the archive has the digest in its .tar.sha256 file (the file only says what the producer wrote: compare the digest with a value from elsewhere)
argv: import hashlib,sys; a,b=sys.argv[1:3]; want=open(b,encoding='utf-8').read().split()[0]; got=hashlib.sha256(open(a,'rb').read()).hexdigest(); sys.exit(0 if got==want else 'the archive does not have the digest in '+b)

The separate browser step: downloads Chromium (not part of the bundle; the archives and the unpacked tree are checked against the bundle's pin) and the operating system libraries it needs (not covered by the pin)

check.title: Re-verify the evidence bundle from the bundle alone, in a process of its own (exit status 0 for an accepted run that verified every assertion, 5 for any finding)

uninstall.title: Remove the installation directory, and nothing else

evidence.description: The demo writes one evidence bundle, {evidence_dir}/profile-demo, and the check step re-verifies it; no JUnit file is involved.

profiles.uninstall_note: uninstall.sh removes the installation directory (virtual environment, browser directory, launcher) and refuses a directory it did not make. The evidence directory and the operating system packages installed by --with-deps stay.
limitations: CPython 3.12 on Linux x86_64 only. Another Python minor or platform is refused by install.sh; macOS and Windows are not claimed.
No bundle is published and no release exists: the archive comes from a build of the repository or from a workflow run, and its digest is only as trustworthy as the place you obtained it from.

Chromium is downloaded when the browser step runs and is not shipped in the bundle; the bundle pins the sha256 of the archives and the mode, size and sha256 of every file of the unpacked tree, the step refuses an archive that does not match, and doctor checks the installed tree. Not covered: the operating system libraries of --with-deps, and the availability of the download host.

The runner in this release runs plans against the bundled fixture app only; a Robot lane that asks for the kernel layers (`origin-only`) is limited by them and does not start where they are unavailable (`doctor` measures them), and a Robot lane that says `not-enforced` is limited by nothing (see the egress matrix in the runner's README).

`verify` recomputes the verdicts from the evidence bundle in a separate process with the same code the run used; the hash chain inside a bundle is unkeyed, so only a manifest digest (the anchor) obtained from somewhere the producer cannot rewrite, or a signature of it by a key the producer does not hold (optional), shows that a bundle is the one it was taken from or signed. A verified run does not show that the application under test is correct.

The agent-harness and runtime-contracts trees are installed from the bundle at the commits pins.toml names; the name `agent-harness` on the public package index belongs to an unrelated project and is never installed.
